identity.title: POCUS gallbladder: stones, wall thickening, sonographic Murphy sign

technique.how: Curvilinear probe, subcostal or intercostal window (deep inspiration or left lateral decubitus helps). Image the gallbladder in long and short axis: look for mobile echogenic foci with posterior shadowing (stones), measure the anterior wall (>3 mm thick), look for pericholecystic fluid, and press the probe directly over the gallbladder for sonographic Murphy sign.
technique.prerequisites: Ideally fasting; sweep the entire gallbladder including the neck to avoid missing impacted stones; identify the main lobar fissure to confirm the structure.
technique.contraindications: None; limited by bowel gas, obesity and contracted post-prandial gallbladder.

interpretation.positive_finding: Gallstones plus wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid or a sonographic Murphy sign supports acute cholecystitis (EP POCUS sensitivity 0.87, specificity 0.82, LR+ 4.7). Stones alone confirm cholelithiasis (pooled sensitivity 0.90, specificity 0.88).
interpretation.negative_finding: No stones and a thin-walled, non-tender gallbladder makes calculous cholecystitis unlikely (LR- 0.16 for cholecystitis) but does not exclude acalculous cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis or cholangitis.
interpretation.pitfalls: Wall thickening is non-specific (hepatitis, heart failure, hypoalbuminemia, ascites, post-prandial state); duodenal gas, polyps and sludge mimic stones; neck stones are easily missed. Sonographic Murphy sign is unreliable after analgesia.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: start cholecystitis pathway (antibiotics, surgical consult), confirm with formal US if needed. Negative: seek other causes; if fever/jaundice persist, image the ducts (US/MRCP).

estimates.population: 710 symptomatic ED patients across 8 prospective studies of emergency physician-performed ultrasound
estimates.reference_standard: Radiology ultrasound, CT, MRI or surgical findings
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.898/(1-0.880) = 7.48; LR- = (1-0.898)/0.880 = 0.116, from pooled sensitivity and specificity
estimates.quote: pooled estimates for sensitivity and specificity were 89.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 86.4% to 92.5%) and 88.0% (95% CI = 83.7% to 91.4%)

estimates.population: 189 ED patients with suspected cholecystitis scanned by 43 EM residents/attendings (median 2 scans each); 23 pathology-confirmed
estimates.reference_standard: Surgical pathology or clinical follow-up at 2 weeks
estimates.quote: sensitivity 87% (95% confidence interval [CI] 66% to 97%), specificity 82% (95% CI 74% to 88%), positive likelihood ratio 4.7

sources.citation: Ross M, Brown M, McLaughlin K, et al. Emergency physician-performed ultrasound to diagnose cholelithiasis: a systematic review. Acad Emerg Med. 2011;18(3):227-235.
Summers SM, Scruggs W, Menchine MD, et al. A prospective evaluation of emergency department bedside ultrasonography for the detection of acute cholecystitis. Ann Emerg Med. 2010;56(2):114-122.
Trowbridge RL, Rutkowski NK, Shojania KG. Does this patient have acute cholecystitis? JAMA. 2003;289(1):80-86.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a negative POCUS to exclude cholangitis, choledocholithiasis or acalculous cholecystitis in critically ill, septic or jaundiced patients; do not rely on wall thickness alone in cirrhosis, heart failure or hypoalbuminemia.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Fever with jaundice, hypotension or dilated bile duct suggests cholangitis: cultures, IV antibiotics, urgent GI/surgical review for drainage irrespective of gallbladder findings.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Summers 2010 included 43 operators with a median of 2 scans each, so results reflect typical rather than expert EPs; stone detection is more reproducible than wall/Murphy assessment.
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Emergency physician with basic biliary POCUS credentialing (typically 25-50 supervised scans); Summers 2010 operators were EM residents and attendings at an academic ED, Ross 2011 pooled EP-performed scans.

extraction_notes: Both estimates come from abstracts. Ross 2011 pooled sens/spec are for cholelithiasis (not cholecystitis); LRs computed by me from pooled values without CIs. Summers 2010 prevalence computed as 23 confirmed/164 analysed (189 scanned minus 25 excluded) = 0.14. Trowbridge RCE cited as index for the clinical context; no RCE table numbers were accessible. Radiology US in Summers performed similarly (sens 83%, spec 86%).
